scenes.headline: How Nemotron 3.5 Super VL keeps long context cheap
scenes.sub: Mamba-2, a little attention, latent experts, and a vision tower
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ashby! Let's open up NVIDIA's new vision language model, and see why long conversations stay cheap.

scenes.text: Forty Mamba-2 layers squeeze the past into a fixed state. Only eight attention layers keep every token, so the cache grows slowly.
scenes.mark: Only eight attention layers keep every token
scenes.say: Most layers squeeze the past into a fixed state. Only eight attention layers keep every token, so the cache grows slowly.

scenes.title: One token's trip through the model

steps.say: Pictures go through a C-RADIO vision tower. A pixel shuffle folds four patches into one token.
Mamba-2 layers carry a fixed-size state, the same at the tenth token and the millionth.
After each mixer comes a mixture of experts. Each token visits twenty-two of five hundred and twelve.
Just eight attention layers store a key and a value for every token. That is the only memory that grows.
A token arrives four thousand ninety six wide, and the router scores every expert.
Then it is squeezed down to a latent a quarter as wide, and only there do the chosen experts run.
One shared expert always runs, at full width.
The expert sum is projected back up and added in. Quarter width vectors also cut traffic between GPUs.

left.title: Every mixer is attention
left.say: If all forty-eight mixers were attention, a million tokens would need about fifty-one gigabytes of cache.

right.title: This hybrid
items: 8.6 GB of KV, plus a fixed state
right.say: With eight, it is under nine gigabytes, plus a small state that never grows.

scenes.label: of 124.45B stored parameters, summed from the safetensors headers
scenes.note: routed experts are 90.6% of the weights
scenes.say: I summed the weight files. About twelve billion parameters run per token, of a hundred and twenty-four billion stored.

scenes.title: Gigabytes to run it
scenes.note: weights from file sizes, caches from config
scenes.say: LM Studio's seventy gigabytes is the four-bit file. Add vision and a long context, and it is about seventy-three.

scenes.text: Most layers keep a fixed state, experts run in a narrow latent, and only eight layers pay for every token.
scenes.mark: only eight layers pay for every token
scenes.say: Fixed state in most layers, experts in a narrow latent, and only eight layers paying for every token.
A mostly Mamba hybrid, twelve billion active, and seventy gigabytes on your desk.
